chats.answer:
For a 4-channel dash cam under $200, I'd prioritize the Rexing C4, followed by the LAMTTO DC21 if you want to spend less.

One important distinction: some 4-channel cameras record front, rear, left, and right, while others record front, rear, and two interior angles. That matters if you're trying to capture side-swipes or parking damage.

Dash Cam Front and Rear with 64GB Card, 4 Channel Dash Camer…

Budget choice

Four-angle 1080p coverage, Wi-Fi, night-vision features and loop recording. Less established brand, so reliability is a bigger question.

Walmart listing

My recommendation

Get the Rexing C4 at $199.99 if your priority is capturing incidents around all four sides of the vehicle. It has a more recognizable brand behind it than many of the inexpensive 360° models, although I haven't verified its long-term reliability through independent testing.

At this budget, expect compromises in nighttime license-plate readability. Also, parking surveillance typically requires hardwiring, and side-facing lenses mounted inside the car may not capture everything outside.

One question: Which type of 4-channel coverage do you want?

Front + rear + left side + right side (exterior protection)
Front + rear + front cabin + rear cabin (rideshare/interior protection)
